project.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

ground_truth.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

parsed_output.evidence:
Root cause / sink: util/src/main/java/io/kubernetes/client/Copy.java:140, inside Copy#copyDirectoryFromPod — `File f = new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName());`. Trust boundary: `entry.getName()` originates from a TarArchiveEntry parsed out of the byte stream returned by `tar cz - <srcPath> | base64` executed *inside the remote pod/container* (Copy.java:123-130) — a compromised or malicious container is fully in control of these entry names, yet the client treats them as safe local filesystem path fragments. From this single unsanitized `f`, two distinct sinks are reachable and both must be fixed:
  1. Copy.java:140/142 — directory-entry path: `if (!f.isDirectory() && !f.mkdirs())` creates attacker-chosen directories directly from the traversal-laden `f`.
  2. Copy.java:140/146/147 — file-entry path: `File parent = f.getParentFile(); ... parent.mkdirs();` followed by `new FileOutputStream(f)` at line 150, creating attacker-chosen parent directories and writing attacker-controlled file content to an attacker-chosen path outside `destination`.
Both sinks were reproduced live: the PoV run shows `escaped file exists = true`, `escaped file outside dest = true`, `escaped file marker matches = true`, `escaped dir exists = true`, `escaped dir outside dest = true`, and exits 0. I additionally verified the negative control: adding a canonical-path containment check right after line 140 (throwing IOException when the resolved path escapes `destination`) causes the same PoV command to exit 1 (`copyDirectoryFromPod threw = true`, no escaped files/dirs), confirming the PoV is a faithful before/after gate for this vulnerability.
parsed_output.expected_vulnerable_behavior: On unpatched code, Copy.copyDirectoryFromPod(...) extracts a tar entry named "../pov-tarslip-escaped-file.txt" and a tar entry named "../pov-tarslip-escaped-dir/" to paths one directory level *above* the caller-supplied `destination` directory (i.e. outside the intended extraction sandbox), because Copy.java:140 does `new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName())` with no canonicalization/containment check before using that File to create directories (line 142, line 147) or write file content (line 150). The PoV verifies the escaped file exists outside `destination`, contains the expected marker content, and the escaped directory exists outside `destination`, then exits 0. The run_pov.sh wrapper builds the `util` module (and its client-java-api/client-java-proto deps) with Maven, compiles CopyTarSlipPov.java against the resulting classpath, and runs it.
parsed_output.notes: The alert contains two traces that share one root cause (Copy.java:140 `new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName())`) fanning out to two sinks: trace 1 ends at line 142 (directory-entry mkdirs) and trace 2 ends at line 147 (file-entry parent.mkdirs(), followed by the write at line 150). I targeted the shared root cause directly and crafted the malicious tar payload to contain both a malicious directory entry and a malicious file entry in the same run, so the single PoV command exercises and verifies both sinks/traces in one shot (see the two escaped-file / escaped-dir assertions in the PoV output). I chose to exercise Copy.copyDirectoryFromPod(...) itself (rather than a synthetic unit test of a helper) by subclassing Copy and overriding only the inherited `exec(...)` transport call — the same technique the project's own CopyTest.java uses (there via WireMock) to avoid a live pod/websocket — so the tar-parsing and file/directory creation logic exercised is 100% real, unmodified production code. I validated the PoV's before/after gating by temporarily patching Copy.java with a canonical-path containment check and confirming the identical `run_pov.sh` command flips from exit 0 (vulnerable) to exit 1 (fixed), then reverted that temporary patch — the worktree's tracked files are unmodified; only `.security-pipeline/pov/` was added.
parsed_output.regression_hint:
Invariant a correct fix must enforce: for every ArchiveEntry extracted in Copy#copyDirectoryFromPod, the canonical path of `new File(destination, entry.getName())` must be equal to, or a descendant of, the canonical path of `destination` — computed and checked *before* any filesystem mutation (mkdirs for directory entries at line 142, parent.mkdirs()+FileOutputStream for file entries at lines 146-150). Reject (or skip with a logged error) any entry that fails this check rather than silently rewriting/stripping the traversal segments, since a bespoke string-strip (e.g. only removing "../" prefixes) is easy to bypass. Known bypass variants the fix must also block, since they all reach the same `new File(destination, entry.getName())` sink:
  - Nested/repeated traversal: "a/../../evil.txt", "../../../../etc/cron.d/x".
  - Absolute path entry names: "/etc/passwd" or Windows-style "C:\\evil.txt" (`new File(dir, "/etc/passwd")` on many platforms yields "/etc/passwd", ignoring `dir` entirely).
  - Symlink entries (TarArchiveEntry.isSymbolicLink()) whose *link target* points outside destination — a pure name-based containment check on the entry name does not prevent a benign-looking entry name from later being written through a previously-planted malicious symlink.
  - Directory entries using the same traversal trick (must be checked identically to file entries — do not special-case the isDirectory() branch out of the containment check).
  - Case/encoding variants on case-insensitive or Unicode-normalizing filesystems.
  - Sibling call site with the identical unguarded pattern potential in copyFileToPod's inverse direction is out of scope here (that path writes a single explicit destPath, not entry-name-derived paths), but any other tar/zip extraction loop added to this client in the future should reuse a single shared, tested "safe extract" helper rather than re-implementing the `new File(dir, name)` pattern.
parsed_output.summary: Created a real PoV (CopyTarSlipPov.java) that drives io.kubernetes.client.Copy#copyDirectoryFromPod through its actual tar/gzip/base64 extraction loop with a crafted malicious tar stream containing entries named "../pov-tarslip-escaped-file.txt" (a regular file) and "../pov-tarslip-escaped-dir/" (a directory). The unmodified production code at Copy.java:140 builds `new File(destination, entry.getName())` without sanitizing the traversal segments, so both a file and a directory are created one level above the caller-supplied destination directory (tar-slip / CWE-22). The PoV subclasses Copy and overrides only the inherited `exec(...)` transport method (the same seam CopyTest.java already relies on) to feed back the malicious tar bytes in place of a real pod exec response; every byte of extraction logic exercised (Base64InputStream -> GzipCompressorInputStream -> TarArchiveInputStream -> new File(...) -> mkdirs()/FileOutputStream) is the real, unmodified Copy.java code.

parsed_output.patch_notes:
Root cause: `Copy#copyDirectoryFromPod` built `File f = new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName())` directly from an untrusted TarArchiveEntry name streamed back from `tar cz - <srcPath> | base64` executed inside the target pod/container, with no containment check before using `f` for `mkdirs()` (directory entries) or `f.getParentFile().mkdirs()` + `FileOutputStream(f)` (file entries).

Fix: replaced the raw `new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName())` construction with a new private helper `resolveEntry(File destinationDir, String entryName)` that:
1. Builds the candidate File the same way as before.
2. Computes `getCanonicalPath()` of both the destination directory and the candidate file (which also resolves any symlinks in intermediate path components, closing the symlink-parent bypass noted in the alert).
3. Throws `IOException` if the canonical target path is not equal to, or a descendant of, the canonical destination path — before any directory creation or file write happens.

This single fix point sits upstream of both sinks named in the alert (line 142 `mkdirs()` for directory entries, and lines 146-150 `parent.mkdirs()` + `FileOutputStream` for file entries), so both trace fans are blocked by one change, along with same-class bypass variants: nested/repeated `..` traversal, absolute path entry names (`new File(dir, "/etc/passwd")`), and case/encoding variants — since canonicalization normalizes all of these before the containment comparison.

Test: added `CopyTest#testCopyDirectoryFromPodRejectsTarSlipEntries`, which reuses the project's existing pattern (subclassing `Copy` and overriding only the inherited `exec(...)` transport call, as `CopyTest` already does via WireMock/thread tricks) to feed a crafted malicious tar/gzip/base64 stream containing a `../pwned-file.txt` file entry and a `../pwned-dir/` directory entry through the real, unmodified extraction loop. Asserts `copyDirectoryFromPod` throws `IOException` and that neither escaped path is created outside the destination directory. Confirmed the finder's PoV (`.security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh`) flips from exit 0 (vulnerable) to exit 1 (safe) with the patch applied, and the full `util` module test suite (146 tests) plus package build both pass.
parsed_output.risk_notes: Low risk: the change only adds a validation check before existing filesystem operations in one method; it does not alter behavior for well-formed (non-traversal) tar entries, which is exactly what the pre-existing CopyTest cases and the new regression test confirm. `copyDirectoryFromPod` already declares `throws IOException`, so surfacing a rejected entry as an `IOException` is consistent with its existing contract and requires no signature changes. The `copyFileToPod` (upload) path is unaffected — it writes to an explicit caller-supplied destPath, not entry-name-derived paths, and was out of scope per the alert.
parsed_output.summary: Fixed CWE-22 tar-slip path traversal in Copy#copyDirectoryFromPod by adding a canonical-path containment check at the shared root-cause sink (Copy.java:140) before any filesystem mutation, so both the directory-entry mkdirs() path (line 142) and the file-entry parent.mkdirs()/FileOutputStream path (lines 146-150) are protected.

parsed_output.diff_review: patch_only.diff touches exactly two files: util/src/main/java/io/kubernetes/client/Copy.java and util/src/test/java/io/kubernetes/client/CopyTest.java. The production change replaces the raw `new File(destination.toFile(), entry.getName())` with `resolveEntry(destination.toFile(), entry.getName())`, a small private static helper that builds the candidate File the same way, computes canonical paths of both the destination directory and the candidate, and throws IOException if the target's canonical path is not equal to or a descendant of the destination's canonical path. This is applied upstream of both sinks named in the alert (line 142 directory mkdirs, and lines 146-150 file parent.mkdirs()+FileOutputStream), so one fix point covers both alert traces. Using getCanonicalPath() (rather than a naive string strip of "../") also defeats nested/repeated traversal, absolute-path entry names (Java's File(parent,child) resolution ignores parent for absolute child on Unix, but the post-construction canonical-path check still catches the escape), and symlink-based redirection of an already-created path component, matching the regression_hint's bypass list. The test-file diff only adds a new regression test (testCopyDirectoryFromPodRejectsTarSlipEntries) plus supporting helpers; it does not modify or weaken any existing test, and does not touch the PoV itself (pov.diff is a wholly separate diff that only adds new files under .security-pipeline/pov/, none of which were altered by the patch). No unrelated or overly broad changes are present — the diff is minimal and precisely scoped to the vulnerability.

parsed_output.summary: The patch adds a canonical-path containment check (resolveEntry helper) at the single shared root-cause sink in Copy#copyDirectoryFromPod (Copy.java:140) before any filesystem mutation, throwing IOException for tar entries whose resolved path escapes the destination directory. This directly closes both alert traces (directory mkdirs at line 142 and file parent.mkdirs()/FileOutputStream at lines 146-150). The PoV flips from vulnerable (exit 0) to safe (exit 1, entry rejected with a clear IOException) after the patch, and the full util module test suite (146 tests, including the existing CopyTest and a new tar-slip regression test) passes with no failures.
